=== DESIGN DOC: our-review-dimensions-v3.md ===

# rebar plan-review gate — design v3 (polyglot re-baseline + reworked anti-FP, one wave)

Supersedes v2. Folds both gap reports + both research rounds (scoping/anti-FP + prior-art diff).
Full DSO citations: dso-dimension-catalog-v2.md.

## FRAMING (corrected)
A rebar FEATURE used by a BROAD, DIVERSE CLIENT BASE — many languages, frameworks, project structures.
Judge every dimension by **cross-language generalization**, not by rebar's own codebase. (Correction: rebar is
Python with legacy bash being strangled out; the earlier "rebar is heavily bash" rationale was a conflation
with DSO and is DELETED.) Fires at open→in_progress; `claim` = fast signed-attestation check; heavy review
out-of-band; it is a REVIEW PROCESS, not a dialog — the CLIENT revises + re-runs to earn a fresh signature.
Reviews a plan an LLM/agent will EXECUTE. Acceptance criteria must be AGENT-COMPLETABLE-IN-SESSION (external
ops OK with provided auth; NO real-user/long-wait/host-live validation).

================================================================
## 0 — ARCHITECTURE: extensible dimension registry (designed to GROW)
================================================================
A dimension = a declarative **registry descriptor**, not bespoke code; the orchestrator is generic (never names
a dimension). Descriptor: `{id, name, scenario, kind(sound|judgment), exec(DET|1-TURN|2-STEP|AGENT),
routing(base|container|leaf|overlay), trigger, tools, impl(DET fn | prompt-file), checklist(binary items),
contract(verdict+findings), severity-policy, block-policy, config}`. Add/remove/tune = edit registry + drop a
prompt/check file; no orchestrator change; schema-validated for reliability. **Reuse rebar's existing
`rebar.llm` extension points** (reviewer catalog.json + contracts.py + prompt files + pluggable runner).
NOTE (prior-art): per-dimension registry + generic orchestrator is UNIQUE in the field (surveyed tools are
monolithic-holistic single prompts or hard-coded persona panels) — it's our growth substrate, and a real bet.
ONE WAVE: all dimensions ship; decomposed into appropriately-sized tasks with dependencies (no v1/deferred).
FUTURE SEAM (design-for, not built this epic): project-supplied dimensions loaded from `.rebar/` config;
project-invariant compliance (a project's own house rules) is the first such — registry shaped to accept it.

================================================================
## 1 — SHARED BASE: anti-FP contract for PLAN review (reworked; every judgment dim inherits)
================================================================
DROPPED (code/diff-review-specific, don't transfer): cite-or-omit-as-universal-gate; reachable-harm bar.
REPLACEMENTS (evidence-grounded — AbsenceBench 2506.11440, CheckEval, TICKing 2410.03608, Agent GPA 2510.08847):
- **Binary-checklist decomposition.** Each dimension = pre-registered binary yes/no checks, NOT 1-5 scalar
  scores (scalar trait scores are LESS human-aligned; binary checks raise agreement, cut variance, and make
  omission-detection tractable). E.g. "Names a failing test per AC: Y/N", "Provides a rollback step: Y/N".
- **MISSING-vs-WRONG routing** (LLMs are good at WRONG, bad at MISSING — AbsenceBench ~70% F1):
  - WRONG (asserts the plan/codebase contains something flawed) → **cite the plan text / codebase fact** (the
    surviving, narrow form of cite-or-omit) — reliable.
  - MISSING (omission) → **never ask open-ended "what's missing"**; pre-derive the EXPECTED-element set, test
    presence as binary checks, **ground the finding in the REQUIREMENT** that makes the element necessary
    ("AC block mandatory for type=task; absent"), apply the **anti-false-omission guard** (search the
    plan/codebase to confirm truly absent before flagging), heavier filtering + abstention (omissions default high-FP).
- **Blockingness-severity** (replaces reachable-harm): Critical = agent can't proceed / will build the wrong
  thing; Major = required element absent → rework; Minor = present-but-thin. Plan-risk is CAPPED (no P0 from
  not-yet-running code). Maps to rebar validate buckets critical/major/minor/warning.
- **Benign-reading filter** (single-pass adjudicator, NOT multi-round debate — debate rewards persuasion over
  truth, 2509.05396): "is there a plausible reading under which this isn't a problem? if yes → drop/downgrade."
- **Anti-fabrication instruction:** "Do NOT invent findings to look thorough; an empty category → 'nothing found'."
- **Calibrated abstention:** confidence per finding; surface only above a threshold calibrated on a small human
  gold set (N≈5-10 corrects systematic bias); abstain (don't fabricate) below. Track BOTH FPR and FNR (two-sided).
- **Single-question scoping + ONE coherence pass (HYBRID).** Per-dimension judges (low cross-talk/FP, actionable)
  PLUS one dedicated cross-dimension **coherence pass** whose only job is contradictions BETWEEN sections
  (e.g. testing strategy vs decomposition; sequencing vs declared dependencies) — single structured check, not debate.
- **Behavioral-test carve-out** (reframed rationale): structural-greps + command-output assertions are a
  LEGITIMATE CROSS-LANGUAGE test pattern (any stack's shell tests) — don't false-flag them as weak tests.
- Reference/exemplar grounding where a gold template/exemplar plan exists (reduces drift+FP).
VERDICT MODEL: per-dim PASS / AMBIGUOUS / FAIL. AMBIGUOUS = non-blocking → escalate to higher-tier adjudicator.
FAIL→block is per-dim, DATA-EARNED: DET/sound checks block immediately (near-0 FP); judgment dims start
escalate/advise, graduate to block only once measured FPR clears the bar (the calibration above).

================================================================
## 2 — DETERMINISTIC TOOLING (fail-open is an IRONCLAD invariant)
================================================================
solidlsp (Serena LSP, already in repo) + ast-grep backstop (P2 resolution, G1 callers, P5 shared-symbol);
syft + per-ecosystem registry HTTP + LLM-fallback (P3 deps); scc + lizard (P4 size/CCN); ast-grep/tree-sitter (G2 locus).
FAIL-OPEN CONTRACT (load-bearing for the diverse client base): capability map; unsupported lang / no server /
crash / timeout / no registry shim → `skipped` = PASS, NEVER a FAIL. Hard "missing" ONLY from a top-tier server
(pyright/gopls/rust-analyzer/tsserver/clangd); weak/absent server → "could-not-confirm". This is the ONLY reason
the deterministic tier generalizes across languages — the invariant must never be violated. Avoid stack-graphs
(archived), Glean (over-engineered); osv-scanner ≠ existence oracle.

================================================================
## 3 — DIMENSION REGISTRY (all ship; one wave)
================================================================
### Tier 0 — DET prefilter (fail-open)
- P1 Readiness shape (standardized `## Acceptance Criteria` all types)
- P2 File/symbol/import resolution (solidlsp+ast-grep)
- P3 Package existence (syft + registry + LLM-fallback)
- P4 Oversize signals (AC/file_impact counts, conjunction/CRUD verbs, layers/interfaces; scc/lizard; config-tunable)
- P5 Task-DAG validity + cross-task interference (shared file/symbol/DB-table/config-key/output-format)
- P6 AC/DD quality: compound-AND split · 9-word vague lexicon · spec-fidelity ≥80% word-overlap · verify-command
  robustness — **POLYGLOT FIX: the grep-anchor/shell-escape/argv-vs-help sub-checks are POSIX-shell-only →
  fail-open/advisory when the verify command isn't a POSIX shell invocation (don't FAIL a `pytest`/`go test`/Makefile
  command for lacking a grep anchor). The CONCEPT (verify-cmd asserts the right thing) is the polyglot part.**
- P7 Destructive/irreversible sniff → escalation to T4 (never pass/fail)

### Tier 1 — judgment, 1-TURN / 2-STEP (binary-checklist; inherit §1)
- F1 Criteria measurability & agent-in-session-completability (+ verify-cmd judgment remainder; + context-window-fit framing)
- F4 User/problem present (light content check)
- E1 Criteria↔description coherence + every-criterion-maps-to-a-step + **intra-plan terminology consistency** + **duplicate/near-duplicate requirement detection** (NEW, Spec Kit)
- E2 Ambiguity / executable-without-clarification (+ spike/research/TBD undercooked + **explicit decision-deferral = finding** — "choose an appropriate X" delegated to the executor, NEW anvil)
- E3 Intent fidelity — 2-STEP blind-restate → compare (child-vs-slice)
- E5 Testing-plan completeness (behavioral+contractual gaps, change-detector avoidance, failure-path + boundary coverage, RED-before-GREEN ordering)
- E6 Verification/termination completeness (per-step codebase-green/testable atomicity; RED→impl edge; + **end-state reachability**: does the union of steps actually reach the stated AC end-state? NEW Simmer — connects to collective-AC-sufficiency)
- G5 Decomposition judgment (too-big/should-have-children; vertical-slice vs horizontal-layer; context-window splittability; consumes P4)

### Tier 2 — judgment, AGENT (tool-grounded, primed by DET tools, fail-open; inherit §1)
- E4 Assumption/premise verification: DET hedge/assertion phrase-scan → FORCED codebase probe per named source (ban cached-context) + benign-reading filter
- G1+G2 Edit-set/scope accuracy: edit-target first (modify=verify locus / create=verify placement) → deterministic consumer/reference lookup (incl. rename/deprecate enumeration completeness); hallucinated+missing; high-blast≠fail
- G3 Child coverage — 4-bucket audit (fully/partial/uncovered/structural) + verbatim 3-condition standard + mandatory coverage map [container]
- G4 Child consistency — all 7 categories (implicit_shared_state/conflicting_assumptions/dependency_gap/scope_overlap/ordering/consumer_impact/residual_refs) [container]
- A1 Anti-slop / over-engineering: NIH (rebuilds existing) · config-surface-proliferation · gratuitous-abstraction (Rule-of-Three call-site count) — codebase-grounded (NOW SHIPS — core in surveyed tools)

### Tier 3 — triggered overlays (router-LLM selects RELEVANCE; overlay judges ADEQUACY)
- T1 Prior-art / novel-architecture justification (+ anti-repackaging, + Rule-of-Three) [web]
- T2 Empirical probe (red→green / spike)
- T3 Integration feasibility (+ CLI --help subcommand-inventory + assumed-vs-actual diff + auth-HTTPS precond + deprecated-API)
- T4 Compat/destructiveness as EXPLICIT JUSTIFIED CHOICE (bidirectional: unacknowledged breakage AND gratuitous compat/flags; expand-contract sequencing; rollback path)
- T5a Performance / T5b Reliability (blast-radius-only-lowers) / T5c Security (ambiguity-not-absence) / T5d Accessibility / T5e Maintainability (coupling + changeability)
- T6 UX non-happy-path
- T7 Documentation (new-needed + existing-invalidated + not-excessive/non-navigable + hot-path-instruction-bloat)
- T8 LLM/prompt antipatterns (bot-psychologist taxonomy)
- T9 Shared-state lifecycle (CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME/RETIRE)

### Cross-cutting
- Router-LLM triage (overlay relevance; DET priors; recall-biased) · coherence pass (§1) · benign-reading adjudicator
  · verdict aggregation · attestation signing + invalidation-on-edit · per-dim FPR/FNR calibration.

================================================================
## 4 — DISTINCTIVE BETS (ahead of field; Opus to pressure-test whether worth the complexity)
================================================================
extensible registry+generic orchestrator · DET-tooling tier w/ fail-open (only grounded-in-tools critic found) ·
signed attestation + invalidation + close-gate enforcement · blind-restate E3 · router w/ DET priors ·
forced-probe E4 (most aggressive assumption-verification in the set) · G3/G4 child audits (no tool does the 7
cross-child modes) · verify-cmd-robustness P6 (must stay polyglot).

================================================================
## 5 — OUT OF SCOPE (confirmed)
================================================================
F2/F3 cross-ticket overlap/dependency (deterministic file-impact/link now; semantic backlog-scan → follow-on) ·
propose-multiple-then-select loop (authoring) · cross-service deploy topology (not in-session-verifiable) ·
DSO dogfooding/staged-rollout/7-day validation (violates agent-completable) · all-equal-5 / scalar-trait gating
(use binary checks + dimension VALUES) · structured-I/O inter-step handoff contract (authoring concern) ·
project-supplied dimensions (FUTURE seam, design-for not built).

## OPEN
- Per-dim block-policy = data-earned (DET blocks now; judgment dims escalate→block on measured FPR). Confirmed-direction.
- Coherence-pass + binary-checklist decomposition are NEW since v2 — Opus review to pressure-test.

comments.body:
=== DESIGN DOC: plan-review-design.md ===

# rebar plan-review gate — consolidated reviewer design (DRAFT for validation)

Synthesis of three research streams: DSO dimension extraction (primary), GitHub
ecosystem cross-check, and LLM-planning failure-mode mapping. Organized onto Joe's
proposed model: **a base set of always-on reviewers (chunked into low-false-positive
single-dimension questions a Sonnet agent answers reliably), plus overlay reviewers
triggered by base-reviewer output OR deterministic ticket analysis.**

DSO citations are relative to `~/digital-service-orchestra/plugins/dso/`.

## Settled architecture (prior turns)
- Fires on open→in_progress; `claim` is a FAST check for a valid signed plan-review
  attestation; absent/stale → fail with `--force`+justification override (recorded).
- Heavy review is a separate out-of-band step (separate critic ≠ author).
- Routing pivots on `has_children` (not ticket type).
- Attestation binds to latest **material** event commit on the tickets branch
  (scope (i): description, AC/success criteria, plan, file_impact, child set+criteria).
- Block on sound/mechanical checks; advise (durably recorded, overridable) on LLM judgment.
- Triaged: cheap deterministic triage → base panel → tier-gated expensive overlays.

---

## BASE REVIEWERS — always run, one dimension per call, tuned for near-zero FP

### Deterministic floor (Layer 1, hard-fails claim; no LLM)
- **B0 Readiness shape.** `has_children` XOR `has_plan`; `## Acceptance Criteria`
  present. Neither plan nor children → FAIL ("add plan or decompose"). Sound check.
  - DSO: type-detection gates (brainstorm SKILL.md:83-112) generalized to has_children.
  - GitHub Tier A: completeness. Failure mode: n/a (structural).

### Always-on LLM chunks (advisory, recorded; each a single narrow question)
- **B1 File-reference resolution (SOUND).** Every path/symbol/import the plan names
  resolves in the repo (grep/LSP); flag nonexistent references. Near-zero FP.
  - NOTE (validation): this is an EXTENSION beyond DSO. DSO's inference-signal scan
    (epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:65-84) is targeted — it triggers on hedging/assertion
    trigger words then MUST-verifies *that* source, not a blanket "resolve everything."
    Our always-on resolve-all framing is our generalization (safe: it's sound/tool-grounded).
  - DSO: inference-signal scan (epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:65-84); feasibility CLI
    `--help` match (feasibility-reviewer.md:65). GitHub Tier A: feasibility.
  - Failure mode #2 (nonexistent symbol/API/package; ~1/3 of repo hallucinations, 2409.20550).
  - **Scenario 3.**
- **B2 Criteria↔description coherence (advisory, framed as coverage not quality).**
  Does every described unit of work map to a criterion, and every criterion to
  described work? No silent drops/contradictions. Chunked as bidirectional coverage.
  - DSO: SC-contradiction (preplanning/SKILL.md:880); spec-fidelity ≥80% (preplanning/SKILL.md:938);
    verify-intent completeness (verifiable-sc-check.md:78-85). GitHub Tier A: traceability.
  - Failure mode #1 (intent) partial. **Scenario 7.**
- **B3 Ambiguity / executable-without-clarification.** Undefined terms, unstated
  decisions, placeholder language ("TBD"/"verify whether"/"check if") that force the
  agent to guess. Deterministic keyword scan + LLM for semantic ambiguity.
  - DSO: agent-clarity `self_contained` (agent-clarity.md:23); scope-bullet concreteness
    (brainstorm SKILL.md:244); ambiguity scan 6 signals (implementation-plan SKILL.md:290-298).
  - GitHub Tier A: clarity/unambiguity (most universal). Failure mode #16 (fail-to-clarify, 11.7% MAST).
  - **Scenario 2.**
- **B4 Intent fidelity (advisory, highest value).** Reviewer restates the goal from
  the plan/children alone; does it match the ticket's stated problem/AC? Flag mismatch.
  - DSO: value `user_impact` (value.md:24); agent-clarity self_contained.
  - GitHub Tier A (intent). Failure mode #1 (semantic misunderstanding, 27% Plan-and-Solve —
    dominant class, NOT fixed by prompt structure). CoVe-style: judge from plan, not its justification.

---

## CONTAINER BRANCH (has_children) — base additions

- **C1 Child coverage (advisory; constructive+adversarial pair).** Every parent
  criterion maps to ≥1 child; union of children covers parent w/o gaps; no child
  exceeds parent scope. DSO's strongest, most-redundant chain.
  - DSO: SC→DD coverage audit protocol + standard (red-team-reviewer.md:156-171);
    story-decomposer sc_coverage_plan (preplanning/SKILL.md:447); dd_collective_ac_coverage (completeness.md:26).
  - GitHub Tier A: traceability. **Scenario 8.**
- **C2 Child consistency.** Children conflict: shared state w/o dep, contradictory
  assumptions, ordering/dependency gaps, scope overlaps, unenumerated residual refs.
  - DSO: red-team story_review 7-category taxonomy (red-team-reviewer.md:190-240).
  - Failure mode #8 (deps/ordering). (Overlaps B/L consumer checks — kept separate.)

## LEAF BRANCH (no children, has plan) — base additions

- **L1 Decomposition / one-shot sizing (HARD-FAIL on deterministic oversize; advisory
  on borderline).** Is this one-shottable or does it need children? Joe's explicit FAIL
  condition: "no children + too big → FAIL, decompose." Deterministic signals (AC count,
  file_impact count, conjunction/CRUD-verb scan, layers/interfaces touched) → hard-fail;
  borderline LLM judgment → advisory (FP risk per research).
  - CRUX (validation e2): `has_children` means "ALREADY decomposed," NOT "needs
    decomposition." A childless ticket can be epic-shaped (multi-persona, UI+backend,
    migration). DSO forces COMPLEX on these via epic-only overrides (complexity-evaluator.md:224-253);
    our routing sends them to the leaf branch, so **L1 is the ONLY thing catching
    "should have been decomposed"** — it must carry the decomposition-pressure signals,
    not just raw size.
  - DSO: 3-gate atomicity (implementation-plan SKILL.md:677-680, dup task-design.md:23);
    scope `right_sized` (scope.md:23); INVEST-Small (preplanning SKILL.md:650);
    complexity-evaluator dims (complexity-evaluator.md). GitHub Tier B: decomposition.
  - Failure mode #21 (granularity). **Scenario 1.**
- **L2 Consumer / blast-radius (SOUND-ish via find-references).** For each symbol/API
  the plan changes, are callers/consumers addressed? Renames enumerate all callers.
  - DSO: consumer_completeness (scope.md:26); scrutiny Part C (epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:88-115);
    red-team consumer-impact + residual-references (red-team-reviewer.md:227-240).
  - Failure mode #3 (blast-radius under-reach; single-file vs multi-file gold, 2310.06770).
  - **Scenario 4.**
- **L3 Test / TDD discipline (advisory + structural).** Plan names failing test(s)
  first (RED→GREEN); covers modified AND removed behavior, not create-only.
  - SUB-SIGNAL (validation e3): a **non-executable / docs-only / instruction-file**
    leaf must be EXEMPT from behavioral-TDD scoring (DSO exempts these: preplanning
    SKILL.md:897; tdd.md instruction-file scoring path tdd.md:44-74). Detect via
    file_impact extensions / no-code signal; else L3 misfires on a docs ticket.
  - DSO: tdd reviewer 7 dims incl. red_green_sequence, bidirectional_test_coverage (tdd.md:80-86);
    TDD Done-of-Done (preplanning SKILL.md:895); completeness e2e_coverage (completeness.md:24).
  - Failure mode #10 (missing tests / verification subversion). **Scenario 5.**
- **L4 Task dependency / ordering / no-coupling (validation c1 — base-worthy, was dropped).**
  For a MULTI-STEP leaf plan: steps form a valid acyclic order; no implicit ordering;
  no two steps silently write the same file/state. DSO runs this always-on on every plan.
  - DSO: Dependencies reviewer `dag_validity`+`no_coupling` (dependencies.md:23-24);
    always-on per review-criteria.md:24. Failure mode #8 (deps/ordering). Sound-ish (graph check).

---

## OVERLAY REVIEWERS — triggered (NOT always-on)

Trigger = deterministic signal (field presence, keyword, size, external ref, tag) OR
a base-reviewer flag. This IS the "tuned for complex/core, skipped for minor" knob.

- **O1 Prior-art / novel-architecture justification.** Trigger: novelty claim in plan,
  new dependency, touches-core keyword/tag, or B-reviewer "novel mechanism" flag.
  Requires: existing alternative named + concrete limitation + measurable advantage +
  prior-art survey (web/GitHub).
  - DSO: justification `divergence_justified` (justification.md:24); web-research warrant
    6 conditions (epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md:165-175). GitHub Tier B: alternatives-considered.
    RFC/PEP "Rationale and alternatives + Prior art". **Scenario 6.**
- **O2 Empirical probe required.** Trigger: risk tier — data migration/schema,
  concurrency, security/auth, public API/contract, novel mechanism. Requires a
  red→green artifact (or spike output) bound to a commit SHA, independently re-runnable.
  - DSO: spike / time-boxed investigation lives in feasibility-reviewer.md:118-127 +
    preplanning walking-skeleton step (NOT gap-analysis.md — corrected: gap-analysis is
    a static cross-task gap taxonomy with no probe/spike concept).
  - LLM-Modulo external grounding (2402.01817); probe-gaming guard (METR/NIST). XP spike /
    walking skeleton / tracer bullet. **Joe's probe idea.**
- **O3 Integration feasibility.** Trigger: external API/service/dependency reference.
  Verify against official docs + working GitHub examples; CLI `--help` surface match.
  - DSO: feasibility-reviewer (whole agent). GitHub Tier A: feasibility.
- **O4 Safety / backward-compat / deploy.** Trigger: migration/schema/destructive/
  rename keywords or tags. Expand-contract, reversibility, drain before destructive.
  - DEPARTURE FROM DSO (validation c2): DSO runs Safety ALWAYS-ON (review-criteria.md:23).
    Keyword-triggering risks missing a destructive op described without trigger words —
    consider keeping a cheap always-on "destructive/irreversible?" sniff that escalates to O4.
  - DSO: safety.md; reliability error_handling/failover (reliability.md). GitHub Tier C: rollback.
  - Failure mode #20 (missing migration/backfill).
- **O5 UX non-happy-path.** Trigger: UI intent signal. Validation errors, timeouts,
  empty/partial states, entry/exit, highest-stakes interactions.
  - DSO: UX probe set (ux-probe-set.md:13-24); testing user_journey_coverage (testing.md:25).
- **O6 Quality-attribute (perf/reliability/security/a11y/maintainability).** Trigger:
  relevant keyword/tier.
  - DESIGN CHANGE, not inheritance (validation d2): DSO runs all 6 board reviewers
    ALWAYS-ON with *conditional findings* (preplanning SKILL.md:498) — the "what to flag"
    column gates whether a FINDING is emitted, not whether the reviewer RUNS. We gate
    whether it runs at all (cost). Watch the maintainability `documentation`/ADR dimension
    (maintainability.md:26) — "new pattern/contract needs documenting?" may be base-worthy.
  - DSO: preplanning Architecture Board (security/performance/accessibility/testing/
    reliability/maintainability reviewers). GitHub Tier B: quality attributes.

---

## DSO LESSONS PRESERVED (rubric content worth keeping)
- Two-column "what good vs bad looks like" rubric tables per dimension.
- "Outcomes not outputs" criteria discipline; verify-intent = subject+action+observable.
- SC→DD→AC traceability chain (here: parent→children→plan→AC).
- 3-gate atomicity definition (testable / codebase-green / max-granularity).
- Verify-command defect taxonomy (8 classes) — reusable for AC verify commands.
- Constructive-vs-adversarial redundancy (decomposer builds, red-team attacks).
- Blast-radius as a tiebreaker that only LOWERS a score, never raises.

## DSO RIGIDITY SHED (explicitly NOT inheriting)
- Fixed magic-number thresholds applied identically to 2-file CLI and payments rewrite
  (≥3 layers, **≥1 interface** [corrected from ≥5 — a single interface change forces
  COMPLEX], >6 SC, ≥7 SC→COMPLEX). → Use signals as inputs to judgment, not bright-line gates.
- "ALL dimensions must equal 5" gating (one 4 fails the plan) — contradicts "a 4 is
  honest". NOTE (validation d1): this all-5 bar is **implementation-plan-skill-specific**;
  every other DSO scored review uses threshold 4. → PASS = no blocking findings, not all-perfect-scores.
- No-substitution HARD-GATEs + mandatory full pipelines regardless of size. → Triage.
- Type-keyed special-casing (epic-only overrides, bug-vs-story forks). → has_children +
  complexity, except preserve bug's reproduction/fix-scope as a complexity sub-signal.
- App-specific hardcoded invariants (ClientFactory/SharedState/...). → Read from project
  config/conventions, not hardcoded.
- Type-absence → max rigor; ceremony/marker bookkeeping entangled with judging.

## OPEN QUESTIONS FOR JOE
1. Base set size: 5 always-on chunks (B1-B4 + branch) + triggered overlays — right cut?
2. Are the DSO "Architecture Board" 6 reviewers correctly demoted to triggered overlays
   (O6), or should any (e.g. testing) be always-on?
3. PASS semantics: "no blocking findings" with advisory findings recorded — confirm.

comments.body:
=== DISCUSSION NARRATIVE (chronological decision log) ===
Brainstorm to design an open->in_progress plan-review verification gate for rebar. One-question-at-a-time
protocol, grounded in subagent research + critique. Below is the decision arc, turn by turn.

[FRAMING] Joe: design a verification workflow that runs when a ticket goes open->in_progress, mirroring the
completion-verifier close gate but harder. Seed scenarios to catch: (1) work too big to one-shot -> decompose;
(2) too ambiguous -> clarify; (3) file references don't match the work; (4) plan ignores upstream/downstream
consumers; (5) plan ignores tests / TDD; (6) novel architecture not validated vs prior art (tuned: required for
complex/core changes, skipped for minor); (7) success-criteria/DoD don't match the description; (8) child tickets
don't fully/accurately cover the parent (evaluated when parent goes in_progress). Generalize across ticket type
and work size. Joe will add scenarios later.

[Q1 - what artifact is reviewed] I challenged: completion-verifier works because at close there's an
implementation to check; at open->in_progress nothing is built, so we judge a SPEC, and scenarios 4/5/6
presuppose a "plan" that may not exist. Joe: it depends on type -> a leaf (task/bug) must contain an
implementation plan (fail if absent); a story/epic may contain a plan OR have children that contain plans; if it
has children, evaluate whether children fully/accurately cover the parent; if neither plan nor children, fail
("add a plan or decompose"); a plan + no children must fail if too big to one-shot. THEN Joe refined: use
HAS_CHILDREN as the routing pivot, not ticket type (more reliable; type only colors prompt emphasis).

[BLOCKING ARCHITECTURE] I raised the hot-path tension (claim is the parallel-agent primitive; a heavy LLM+web
review can't block it inline) and offered A blocking-inline / B advisory / C decoupled-signed-attestation. Joe:
claiming should be a FAST succeed/fail; the process should EMPOWER the agent by surfacing flaws; the reviewer and
the plan-author must be SEPARATE agents (objectivity); also consider requiring empirical PROBES at plan time
(easier for an LLM to observe a real failure than mentally simulate) but only for significant/sensitive work.
I researched: hard-gate-is-anti-pattern does NOT transfer to autonomous agents (agents confabulate vs ask);
errors compound; separate critic >> self-critique (Kambhampati self-verification collapse). Landed on:
decoupled signed "ready" attestation; claim checks it fast.

[ATTESTATION + INVALIDATION] Joe: block on absence of a signed plan review, with an override+justification like
--force-close; invalidate the review if criteria/AC are edited (ticket is non-terminal). I proposed binding
scope; Joe chose scope (i): hash the ticket's own authored fields (description/AC/success-criteria/plan/
file_impact/child-set+criteria); drift detection is a future feature, out of scope. Joe asked whether we can bind
to a commit on the tickets branch -> yes, the git-native form of scope (i); refined to the latest MATERIAL event
commit (ignore comments/tags/links/assignee so progress comments don't force re-review).

[VERDICT/COMPOSITION] I mapped the completion-verifier pattern and proposed block-on-sound / advise-on-judgment.
Joe insisted: define WHAT we measure before WHAT blocks; rejected blocking on deterministic grounds ONLY;
AMBIGUOUS can be non-blocking; FAIL-block is per-dimension TBD (by severity/dimension/FP-likelihood); AMBIGUOUS as
an escalation signal to a higher-tier adjudicator is good; for each dimension consider full-agent-with-tools vs
one-turn eval.

[DSO DEEP-DIVE SAGA] Joe pointed me at the DSO project's brainstorm/preplanning/implementation-plan skills +
prompts + agents to mine hard-won review dimensions ("preserve the lessons without inheriting the rigidity").
First a single big extraction agent -> Joe: it OMITS key dimensions (fidelity reviews, gap analysis,
security/accessibility, red-team, understanding gate). I chunked into 5 agents -> still incomplete. Joe pushed:
diagnose the FLAW in my exploration and re-explore FROM SCRATCH; if a fresh pass misses what we know, the
methodology is broken. I diagnosed two flaws (preselected-location chunking blind to surfaces I didn't name;
lossy consolidation) and built a coverage-ledger methodology: full file inventory (42 skills/53 agents/81 hooks/
160 docs) -> signal grep -> 8 bounded lossless agents, each reconciling against the prior catalog. Result: every
prior dimension CONFIRMED + ~150 new + corrections; surfaced entire missed surfaces (the review HARNESS:
reviewer-base/delta/contracts/tristate-lattice; the gate/hook ENFORCEMENT layer; the Understanding Gate;
cross-epic scan; post-scrutiny handlers; the 13 untouched planning/quality skills).

[PRIOR ART + FAILURE MODES] Parallel research: GitHub LLM-plan-review ecosystem (Spec Kit /analyze 114k*, Kiro,
rfc-reviewer, anvil, flowglad, claude-code-plan-critique); LLM-planning failure-mode taxonomies (MAST ~44%
spec/plan failures; Plan-and-Solve 27% semantic-misunderstanding; TravelPlanner 0.6%; AbsenceBench - LLMs bad at
detecting omissions; Kambhampati 84% false-ACCEPT). Verdict-composition research said: (A) block-on-sound /
advise-on-judgment is the floor; (C) promote a judgment dim to block only once measured <~10% effective-FP;
reject (B) block-by-default-with-routine-override (static-analysis abandonment thresholds: >30% FP -> tool
ignored).

[OPUS CRITICAL REVIEW] An Opus adversarial review of v3 found the load-bearing error: we'd engineered the whole
anti-FP contract against false-POSITIVES while our own evidence says LLM plan-judges fail by false-ACCEPTANCE
(rubber-stamping). Also: cost incoherent (flat fan-out vs the cascade our own research prescribed); fail-open
silently guts the gate for non-mainstream-language clients + the attestation hides that; the 30+ dimension
registry is partly gold-plating with concrete double-flagging; calibrated abstention needs gold data that won't
exist; "agent-completable-in-session" is load-bearing yet unspecified; invalidation-on-edit risks a re-review
treadmill.

[THE REBALANCE - Joe sharpened it] Joe: the false-positive problem I over-indexed on is a CODE-REVIEW problem
(that's where I found the FP prompts in rebar) - NOT what we're designing. Also corrected: rebar is NOT heavily
bash (I'd conflated it with DSO; rebar is Python with legacy bash being strangled) - remediate that. And the
gate serves a BROAD, DIVERSE CLIENT BASE (many languages/frameworks/structures); stop over-indexing on rebar's
own needs. Outcome: RECALL-FIRST rebalance - sound/deterministic checks block, LLM judgment advises/surfaces;
anti-FP stripped to minimal; FNR-on-seeded-bad-plans as primary metric. Dropped cite-or-omit-as-universal-gate
(fails for omissions -> ground the REQUIREMENT instead; AbsenceBench: never ask open-ended "what's missing")
and reachable-harm (no impl at plan time -> blockingness-to-criteria severity). Severity-minor-floor deferred
(code-review concept needing per-criterion tuning). Calibrated abstention dropped (no gold set -> surface-on-
uncertainty). Fail-open is DESIRED; the certificate means "process followed to the best of our ability, no red
flags" - NOT "perfect" - with COVERAGE recorded for transparency.

[CONFIGURABLE CHUNKING - Joe's reconciliation] Single holistic pass optimizes cost over quality; research shows
per-criterion decomposition improves quality (field avoids it only for cost). Joe: split the difference - let
the PROJECT configure CHUNKING (how many criteria per LLM call); local/small-model clients chunk finer (more
smaller calls, less context-limit risk), frontier-model clients chunk coarser (fewer calls, comparable quality);
"in the middle" default. Makes holistic-vs-decomposed a tunable that serves the diverse base.

[LAYER-2 LOOP - Joe's catch] Joe: when does the Layer-2 loop happen? Either the review is re-run from scratch
(then don't limit to prior findings if the plan changed) or it loops within one review (then why a second broad
pass?). Resolution: NO internal refine loop / NO second broad pass; the reviewer runs once per invocation and
returns findings; the only loop is the CLIENT re-invoking after revising. Convergence is FREE because Layer 1
(deterministic frozen binary rubric) is the SOLE blocker - all-MET is a guaranteed fixed point regardless of
advisory findings. On re-run, review the current plan FRESH; diff-only is an optional cost-saver, not a
convergence mechanism. (Convergence research confirmed: cap + severity-gating + diff-only + freeze-rubric; field
keeps LLM plan-review ADVISORY not blocking BECAUSE of the rubber-stamp problem + non-determinism.)

[BUDGET / ESCALATION / PROPORTIONATE / BUGS] Joe: scrutiny must scale with ticket size/complexity (don't give a
small task an epic's review). Budget caps: handle hitting them - criterion/chunk-ATOMIC checkpointing (no
half-criterion waste); on hit -> a NON-TERMINAL "incomplete" outcome (NOT failed - cap is external to the ticket;
NOT certified - process didn't complete); client raises budget / re-runs / escalates. Escalation factors = SIZE
+ COMPLEXITY + CENTRALITY (DSO has hooks/lib/centrality.sh + blast-radius-score.py). Risk posture is
PROJECT-CONFIGURABLE with a sensible default; Joe wants to APPROVE the time/cost/risk tradeoffs. Bugs: park them
- ship with bug-type SKIPPED + a follow-on epic (their format/content differs; bugs often lack a plan at claim
because you investigate first); revisit after tuning; interim has_plan-driven (planless ticket = N/A, not FAIL).

[EXTENSIBILITY] Joe: design to GROW - tuning/adding/removing a dimension must be trivial+reliable. -> a dimension
is a declarative REGISTRY DESCRIPTOR; generic orchestrator; reuse rebar.llm's catalog.json+contracts+prompt+
runner extension points. Project-specific review criteria = a FUTURE SEAM (design-for, not built this epic);
project-invariant compliance is the first such. Implement ALL criteria in ONE WAVE, decomposed into
appropriately-sized tasks with dependencies.

[POLYGLOT TOOLING] Research: semantic resolution (P2/G1) is only honest via LSP-class tools; the happy finding is
solidlsp (Serena's LSP lib) is ALREADY in this repo. Stack: solidlsp + ast-grep (P2/G1/G2), syft + per-ecosystem
registry + LLM-fallback (P3), scc + lizard (P4). FAIL-OPEN is an ironclad invariant (unsupported lang/no server/
crash/timeout -> skipped=PASS, never FAIL; hard "missing" only from top-tier servers). Avoid stack-graphs
(archived) / Glean (over-engineered); osv-scanner != existence oracle.

[DSO TICKET MINING - tuning] Joe: mine DSO's ticket data (rebar-like store) for a temporary example library to
tune complexity-proportionate scrutiny + over/under-review risk. Findings: store is an event-sourced rebar store
(orphan tickets branch + .tickets-tracker/, one dir per ticket, .cache.json head state); ~8,317 native tickets
(task 4455/bug 2112/story 1362/epic 388; ~82% closed). KEY: file_impact is effectively UNUSED (1 ticket);
AC checklists exist mostly on tasks (50%); only 59 tickets carry an in-comment COMPLEXITY label (weak-gold seed,
bug-skewed); signatures/verify_commands sparse. Proposed depth tiers grounded in the distribution (tasks/bugs by
files/layers: <=1 minimal / 2-3 standard / >3 deep; stories/epics by children: 0-1 / 2-6 / >=7); escalation =
size x complexity x centrality (persist blast-radius + centrality scores at plan time - the single highest-
leverage tuning fix); default chunking 3-5 ACs per call. Rework markers correlate with complexity (epics with
>=7 children carry rework markers 42% vs 12% for <7 - validates children>=7 as a deep-review trigger). Honest
limits: labels sparse + bug-skewed, outcomes text-inferred, DSO-specific topology won't transfer cleanly - good
as a TUNING + regression set, not a clean held-out eval set.

[CONVERGED DESIGN - two layers] LAYER 1 deterministic + structural frozen-binary-rubric gate = the ONLY blocker
(convergent by construction); LAYER 2 advisory LLM review (structured criteria, chunking-configurable) + ONE
bounded broad open-ended pass for unknown-unknowns, never blocks, surfaces findings; client revises + re-runs.
Reviewer != the model that authored the plan (self-preference). Cert = process-followed + no-red-flags + coverage;
material-edit invalidation. See the appended design docs (our-review-dimensions-v3.md is the latest; v4
design-of-record pending, to fold in the DSO mining tuning + budget-incomplete status + escalation).

[CORRECTIONS I LOGGED] (1) "rebar is heavily bash" was wrong (conflation with DSO; rebar is Python). (2)
Optimized the wrong loss (FP vs FN) until Joe + Opus corrected it. (3) Over-consolidated DSO extraction twice
before the coverage-ledger re-do. (4) cite-or-omit + reachable-harm were code-review imports, dropped.

[OPEN / NEXT] Write the v4 design-of-record (Layer-1/Layer-2 + configurable chunking + budget-incomplete +
escalation by size/complexity/centrality + DSO-grounded depth tiers). Then decompose into the rebar
implementation epic (one wave, tasks with deps). PENDING JOE: approve the proportionate-depth posture/thresholds,
the budget posture, and confirm bug-skip + follow-on epic.

=== UPDATE: coaching-posture research + final decisions + v4 plan-of-record ===

COACHING-POSTURE RESEARCH (verdict): the "require-basics(deterministic)-then-advise / positive-guidance" posture
is well-supported by 2026 research. KEYSTONE: LLMs can't reliably FIND their own errors but CAN fix them once
given the LOCATION (Tyen et al. ACL'24, 2311.08516) -> the reviewer's job is to SUPPLY the finding+location the
agent can't self-detect; the agent is a competent fixer from there. External feedback beats intrinsic
self-critique (2310.01798, 2402.08115, LLM-Modulo 2402.01817). Rigid SEMANTIC gates get churned/reward-hacked
(SpecBench 2605.21384) -> keep the hard floor MINIMAL+unambiguous; make every semantic judgment ADVISORY.
FEEDBACK-AUTHORING SPEC (per advisory finding): (1) GROUND it in a criterion/file/section (highest-value lever;
in-place located feedback ~doubles fix accuracy vs free-text); (2) SPECIFIC+ACTIONABLE not generic; (3) a
concrete SUGGESTED edit ONLY when confident (a wrong fix regresses BELOW none, 2504.06939); (4) SEVERITY-RANK +
CAP (few prioritized, critical first); (5) AFFIRM what passes (behavior-specific) to suppress over-correction/
churn (FlipFlop: pushback after a CORRECT answer flips ~46%); (6) express as a CHECKLIST + require addressing
each (TICK/STICK 2410.03608, Rubrics-as-Rewards 2507.17746). HONEST GAP: no direct measurement of how often
advisory feedback is IGNORED (advisory-vs-blocking is reasoned design, not measured) -> exactly what our
FP-instrumentation measures on our own data (remediation-rate-per-criterion).

DECISIONS THIS ROUND (Joe's pushback accepted):
- PER-CRITERIA BLOCKING simplified to what we can build honestly: each Layer-2 criterion config = advisory
  (default) | blocking-with-`--force`-override. We do NOT build a true no-override hard gate; a project composes
  one in CI by checking for the signed result (we expose the data; not recommended). DROPPED (-> follow-ons): the
  measured-FP-surfacing guardrail (it only measures --force circumvention, not real FP/remediation; needs tooling
  + human feedback), auto-demote (same), and the confidence/severity-floor for blocking (LLMs bad at self-
  confidence; "can't meet an AC" isn't the only critical defect; fine-tune later on usage data).
- INCOMPLETE-REVIEW knob: outcome INDETERMINATE (not failed - cap is external; not certified - process didn't
  finish; no signature). Whether INDETERMINATE blocks `claim` is a PROJECT KNOB; DEFAULT = non-blocking (cert
  records "incomplete"; claim proceeds with that on record).
- CHUNKING: determined EMPIRICALLY (NOT from DSO's rubric - what we measure is materially different). Run
  chunk-size experiments, N repeats each, find the quality-degradation point; prime with DSO tickets as
  realistic inputs.
- SIGNALS are validated+improved, not trusted: file_impact empty / AC absent -> COACH the agent to add/repair,
  don't penalize. Standardize on `## Acceptance Criteria` across ALL types (stories' DoD / epics' success-
  criteria collapse into ACs). The DSO complexity label is UNVALIDATED evaluator OUTPUT - one input among many,
  never ground truth.
- DSO data role: NOT a threshold source (rebar != DSO; DSO over-tuned to itself). Use it as (a) representative
  sample tickets for "how do we review THIS kind of ticket" discussions, (b) a SIMULATION corpus to test how
  candidate rules redistribute tickets across review levels, (c) priming for the chunk/threshold experiments.
- ROUTING on complexity + has_children (NOT type): rebar reviews tickets from MANY creation styles that are
  inconsistently typed; DSO's strict type discipline is one creation style, not the only one. Anything ported
  from DSO must be Python, polyglot, and a general principle.
- COACHING dual goals: (1) positive guidance to author better plans (require deterministic basics, then advise);
  (2) the signed cert = a composable "rigorous agentic dev vs vibe-coding" signal for CI (review +
  completion-verification + future workflow signatures).

OBSERVABILITY / FP-ANALYSIS SUBSTRATE (cheap, IN-SCOPE; the enabler for the FP follow-ons): decouple cheap
CAPTURE now from offline ANALYSIS later. STORAGE MODEL DECIDED: (a) ATTESTATION/SIGNATURE = a normal reduced
event ON the ticket (head state; what claim checks; reuses signing.py). (b) REVIEW_RESULT (bulky observability:
per-criterion verdicts + FINDING FINGERPRINTS [hash(criterion+normalized location+normalized text)] + model/chunk/
budget/depth metadata + captured-but-untrusted self-confidence + override justifications) = a reducer-IGNORED
SIDECAR EVENT on the ticket (free sync/push + conflict-free union-merge + co-located with the events the analysis
must correlate against: EDIT/STATUS/reopen/completion-verification), NOT folded into head/graph/health (the
session_log out-of-hot-paths treatment at the event-type level; one new bit = reducer skips this type). REJECTED:
single shared ledger file (merge conflicts in a multi-clone auto-pushed store; breaks per-event-file union-merge).
ALTERNATIVE/fallback only if ticket-dir growth bites: a separate per-review-FILE store / `reviews` branch
(conflict-safe, pristine ticket dirs, but a new store + cross-store join). Body kept COMPACT (full plan text
recoverable from the bound commit, never duplicated); old REVIEW_RESULTs compactable/archivable after extraction.
OFFLINE replay+join on ticket_id+fingerprints yields per-criterion fire-rate, REMEDIATION-rate (fingerprint
resolved after a revision = the real "is the advice useful" metric), FP proxy (flagged->overridden/ignored->
ticket closes clean), FN proxy (silent->later reworked), chunk-size quality, confidence-vs-correctness,
depth-tier distribution. Capture only; never aggregate/decide in-system; no human-feedback requirement.

ARTIFACT: plan-of-record-v4.md written (DESIGN OF RECORD; supersedes our-review-dimensions-v3.md), appended to
this log immediately after this entry. Contains: purpose/posture, two-layer architecture, verdict+blocking model,
the feedback-authoring spec, the criteria registry, execution (chunking/tooling/proportionate scrutiny),
convergence, attestation/cert, the observability substrate + storage model, tuning methodology, the FOLLOW-ON
REGISTER (F1-F12, tracked separately), and open/pending-approval items.

NEXT: pending Joe's approval of (proportionate-depth posture + thresholds, budget posture, bug-skip+follow-on),
decompose the v4 plan into the rebar implementation epic (one wave, tasks with deps) tracked in rebar, and create
the follow-on register items F1-F12 as separate linked tickets (discovered_from).

comments.body:
=== DESIGN OF RECORD: plan-of-record-v4.md ===

# rebar Plan-Review Gate — DESIGN OF RECORD (v4)

A verification workflow that runs when a ticket is claimed (open->in_progress), reviewing the ticket's
implementation plan BEFORE an agent executes it — the inverse of the completion-verifier close gate. A rebar
FEATURE used by a BROAD, DIVERSE CLIENT BASE (many languages/frameworks/structures + many ticket-creation
styles). Supersedes our-review-dimensions-v3.md. Full dimension detail: dso-dimension-catalog-v2.md.

================================================================
## 1. PURPOSE / POSTURE
================================================================
TWO COMPLEMENTARY GOALS:
 (1) COACH agents to author better plans via POSITIVE, well-formed guidance — not negative roadblocks. We
     REQUIRE passing a small set of cheap DETERMINISTIC checks, then ADVISE (non-blocking) on where the plan
     falls short. (Research-backed: LLMs can't self-FIND errors but CAN fix them once given the location
     [2311.08516]; rigid semantic gates get churned/reward-hacked [SpecBench 2605.21384]; external well-formed
     feedback beats intrinsic self-critique [2310.01798, 2402.08115, LLM-Modulo 2402.01817].)
 (2) CERTIFY that a review process was followed before implementation. The signed attestation (alongside
     completion-verification + future workflow signatures) is a composable "rigorous agentic development vs
     vibe-coding" signal a CI process can check on a PR.
The review is a PROCESS, not a dialog: it returns a verdict + findings; the CLIENT revises and re-runs to earn a
fresh signature (mirrors completion-verifier). rebar owns review/verdict/findings/signature/invalidation; the
client owns the revise/retry loop.

================================================================
## 2. ARCHITECTURE (two layers)
================================================================
TRIGGER: fires at open->in_progress. `claim` = FAST check for a valid signed attestation; the heavy review runs
OUT-OF-BAND. Routing pivots on HAS_CHILDREN + COMPLEXITY (NOT ticket type — rebar reviews tickets from many
creation styles that are inconsistently typed; DSO's strict type discipline is one style, not the only one).

LAYER 1 — deterministic + structural floor (the ONLY thing that BLOCKS; convergent by construction). Frozen,
unambiguous, cheap, polyglot-where-tooling-exists, fail-open. All-pass is a guaranteed fixed point. Keep it
MINIMAL so there is nothing to game.

LAYER 2 — advisory coaching review (NEVER blocks by default; SURFACES findings authored for remediation). The
judgment criteria + ONE bounded broad open-ended pass for unknown-unknowns. Per-criterion verdicts.

REVIEWER != the model/instance that authored the plan (self-preference). Per-criterion execution is grouped into
chunks per project config (see #6), not one-agent-per-criterion and not a single monolithic pass.

================================================================
## 3. VERDICT MODEL + BLOCKING
================================================================
Per-criterion: PASS / AMBIGUOUS / FAIL. Plus a review-level INDETERMINATE.
- Layer-1 (sound) FAIL -> BLOCKS (facts; near-zero FP; no override needed, though a project may allow one).
- Layer-2 (judgment) FINDINGS -> ADVISORY by default (surface, don't block). AMBIGUOUS = non-blocking ->
  escalate to a higher-tier adjudicator. Reflect "coach, don't penalize."
- PER-CRITERION BLOCKING KNOB (project config): a project may set a Layer-2 criterion to BLOCKING. Blocking
  means BLOCK-WITH-`--force`-OVERRIDE (recorded justification) — friction without deadlock. We do NOT build a
  true no-override hard gate; a project that insists composes one in CI by checking for the signed result (we
  expose the data; not recommended, and the reasons are documented). Sound criteria block without needing an
  override.
- INCOMPLETE (budget cap hit, or a sound tool unavailable): outcome = INDETERMINATE. NOT failed (the cap is
  external to the ticket), NOT certified (the process didn't finish), no signature minted. Whether INDETERMINATE
  BLOCKS `claim` is a PROJECT CONFIG KNOB; DEFAULT = non-blocking (the attestation records "review incomplete";
  `claim` proceeds with that on record). (Tri-state INDETERMINATE / gate-unavailable doctrine: couldn't-decide
  is its own state, never silently a pass.)
NOTE (deferred, follow-ons #1-4): measured-FP surfacing, auto-demote on FP ceiling, confidence/severity floors —
all need measurement tooling + usage data we do not build this epic. v1 ships sensible defaults + the knob; the
instrumentation in #11 is what makes those refinements possible later.

================================================================
## 4. COACHING / FEEDBACK-AUTHORING SPEC (every advisory finding)
================================================================
The reviewer SUPPLIES the finding + location the agent cannot self-detect. Author each finding to this shape
(evidence-backed):
 - GROUND it in a specific criterion/file/section (highest-value lever; 2311.08516, 2510.00777).
 - SPECIFIC + ACTIONABLE, not generic (2303.17651).
 - A concrete SUGGESTED edit ONLY when confident, marked as a suggestion (a wrong fix regresses below none; 2504.06939).
 - SEVERITY-RANK + CAP: a few prioritized findings, critical first; not a firehose (position bias).
 - AFFIRM what already passes (behavior-specific, not bare praise) to suppress over-correction/churn (FlipFlop 2311.08596).
 - Express as a CHECKLIST and require the agent to address each item (TICK/STICK 2410.03608; Rubrics-as-Rewards 2507.17746).
PROMPT TO IMPROVE, NOT PENALIZE: where a signal is missing/weak (e.g. file_impact empty, AC absent), COACH the
agent to add/repair it — no single stored signal is trusted as ground truth; the review validates & improves them.

================================================================
## 5. CRITERIA REGISTRY (extensible; frozen-within-a-loop, grown-between-versions)
================================================================
A criterion = a declarative DESCRIPTOR; the orchestrator is generic. Reuse rebar.llm's catalog.json + contracts
+ prompt + runner. Descriptor: {id, name, scenario, kind(sound|judgment), exec(DET|1-TURN|2-STEP|AGENT),
routing(base|container|leaf|overlay), trigger, tools, checklist(binary where it decomposes cleanly; graded/
narrative where genuinely qualitative), block_policy(advisory[default] | blocking-with-override), config}.
Implement the full criteria set in ONE WAVE, decomposed into appropriately-sized tasks with dependencies.

LAYER 1 (DET, blocks, fail-open): P1 readiness shape (standardized `## Acceptance Criteria` ALL types) · P2
file/symbol/import resolution (LSP/ast-grep) · P3 package existence (syft+registry+LLM-fallback) · P4 oversize
signals · P5 task-DAG validity + cross-task interference · P6 AC/DD quality (compound-AND, vague-lexicon,
spec-fidelity; verify-command robustness — POSIX-shell sub-checks fail-open/advisory off-shell) · P7
destructive/irreversible sniff (escalation signal only).
LAYER 2 (judgment, advisory): F1 measurability & agent-in-session-completability · F4 user/problem present ·
E1 criteria<->description coherence + terminology-consistency + duplicate-requirement detection · E2 ambiguity
+ undercooked-plan (spike/research/TBD) + explicit-decision-deferral · E3 intent fidelity (2-step blind-restate
-> compare) · E5 testing-plan completeness · E6 verification/termination + end-state-reachability · G1+G2
edit-set/scope accuracy (tool-primed; high-blast != fail) · G3 child coverage (4-bucket + 3-condition) [container]
· G4 child consistency (7 categories) [container] · E4 assumption/premise verification (forced codebase probe)
· A1 anti-slop/NIH/config-proliferation/Rule-of-Three.
TRIGGERED OVERLAYS (router-LLM selects relevance; overlay judges adequacy): T1 prior-art/novel-arch · T2
empirical probe · T3 integration feasibility · T4 compat/destructiveness-as-explicit-choice · T5a-e perf/
reliability/security/a11y/maintainability · T6 UX · T7 documentation (+invalidated +hot-path bloat) · T8
LLM/prompt antipatterns · T9 shared-state lifecycle.
CROSS-CUTTING: ONE coherence pass (cross-section contradictions; single structured check, not debate); ONE
bounded broad open-ended pass (unknown-unknowns; advisory; reviewed once per invocation - no internal loop);
single benign-reading FP filter; anti-fabrication instruction ("empty category -> nothing found").
(All borrowed-from-DSO criteria re-implemented in Python, polyglot, as general principles — DSO over-tuned to
its own project; we keep the principle, drop the DSO-specific tuning.)

================================================================
## 6. EXECUTION: CHUNKING, TOOLING, PROPORTIONATE SCRUTINY
================================================================
CHUNKING (project knob): how many criteria batch per LLM call — local/small-model clients chunk finer (reliable,
context-safe), frontier clients chunk coarser (cheaper, comparable quality). DEFAULT determined EMPIRICALLY (NOT
from DSO's rubric): run chunk-size experiments, N repeats each, find the size where result quality degrades;
prime the experiments with DSO tickets as realistic inputs.
TOOLING (fail-open is an IRONCLAD invariant): solidlsp (Serena, already in repo) + ast-grep (P2/G1/G2); syft +
per-ecosystem registry + LLM-fallback (P3); scc + lizard (P4). Unsupported lang / no server / crash / timeout /
no shim -> skipped = PASS, NEVER FAIL; hard "missing" only from top-tier servers. (This is the only reason the
DET tier generalizes across the diverse client base.)
PROPORTIONATE SCRUTINY: review depth scales with COMPLEXITY + has_children (small task = DET + a light pass;
epic/has_children = full depth). ESCALATION to a stronger model when tier=deep AND (blast-radius high OR
centrality fan-in high OR diff large). COMPUTE + persist centrality + blast-radius at plan time (cheap;
feeds escalation now and seeds the tuning corpus later). RISK POSTURE is project-configurable with a sensible
default; the project owns the time/cost/risk tradeoff. BUDGET CAP per plan (wall-clock + cost); spend at chunk
granularity, checkpoint between chunks (no half-criterion waste), order chunks by priority so a cap sheds the
least-valuable criteria.

================================================================
## 7. CONVERGENCE
================================================================
The only loop is the CLIENT re-invoking after revising. Convergence is FREE because Layer 1 (deterministic,
frozen) is the sole blocker -> all-pass is a guaranteed fixed point regardless of advisory findings. On a re-run
with a changed plan, review the current plan FRESH (do not limit to prior findings). diff-only re-review is an
OPTIONAL cost-saver, not a convergence mechanism. No internal refine loop; no second broad pass within a review.

================================================================
## 8. ATTESTATION / CERTIFICATION
================================================================
The signed attestation = "we ran our process to the best of our ability given this codebase, and no red flags
were raised" — NOT "this plan is perfect." Records COVERAGE (which sound checks ran vs skipped-unsupported) for
transparency. Bound to the latest MATERIAL event commit on the tickets branch (scope (i)): edits to description /
AC / file_impact / decomposition INVALIDATE (re-certify); tags/comments/links/assignee do NOT (no re-review
treadmill). JUSTIFICATION: the cert asserts process-followed-against-THIS-plan; honoring it after a material edit
would falsely certify content never reviewed. The cert is the composable rigor signal for CI (review +
completion-verification + future workflows).

================================================================
## 9. OBSERVABILITY / FP-ANALYSIS SUBSTRATE (cheap, in-scope; the enabler for follow-ons #1-4)
================================================================
Decouple cheap CAPTURE (now) from FP ANALYSIS (offline, later). Leverage event-sourcing.
STORAGE MODEL (decided): TWO artifacts with opposite needs.
 (a) ATTESTATION/SIGNATURE = a NORMAL reduced event ON the ticket (head state; what `claim` checks; reuses the
     close-gate SIGNATURE machinery / signing.py).
 (b) REVIEW_RESULT (bulky observability) = a reducer-IGNORED SIDECAR EVENT on the ticket — stored in the ticket's
     own event stream (free auto-commit/push + conflict-free union-merge + co-located with the events the FP
     analysis must correlate against), but NOT folded into head/.cache and NOT seen by deps/validate/health
     (the session_log out-of-hot-paths treatment applied at the EVENT-TYPE level; the one new bit of machinery =
     the reducer intentionally SKIPS this type, making the existing preserved-and-ignored behavior deliberate).
     REJECTED: a single shared ledger file (line-level merge conflicts in a multi-clone auto-pushed store -
     breaks rebar's per-event-file union-merge convergence). ALTERNATIVE/fallback: a separate per-review-FILE
     store / `reviews` branch (conflict-safe, keeps work-ticket dirs pristine) - but it is a new parallel store
     AND forces a cross-store join; only switch if ticket-dir growth becomes a real problem. NOT one-ticket-per-
     review (heavy ticket-space pollution + relates_to-join instead of co-location).
     Keep the body COMPACT (fingerprints + per-criterion verdicts + short finding text + citation; full plan
     text recoverable from the bound material commit, never duplicated); old REVIEW_RESULT events are
     compactable/archivable after offline extraction (observability, not state).
The REVIEW_RESULT record carries: {review_id, ticket_id, ts, bound material-commit SHA, model+version, depth tier, chunking
config + criterion->chunk map, budget cap/spent, budget-hit; per-criterion: criterion_id, verdict, kind, exec,
blocking-configured, finding text+citation, FINDING FINGERPRINT = hash(criterion + normalized location +
normalized text), model self-reported confidence [captured-but-untrusted, for later study]; overall outcome,
signature-minted; prior review_id if a re-review}. Log `--force` overrides structured (which criteria, reason).
LEAN ON EXISTING EVENTS for the rest (no new tracking): EDIT/material commits, STATUS/reopen/supersede,
completion-verification result. OFFLINE a replay+join (on ticket_id + fingerprints) computes per criterion:
fire rate, REMEDIATION RATE (fingerprint resolved after a revision = the real "is the advice useful" metric),
FP proxy (flagged -> overridden/ignored -> ticket closes clean/CV-PASS/no rework), FN proxy (silent ->
later reworked), chunk-size quality experiments, confidence-vs-correctness, depth-tier distribution. CAPTURE
ONLY — never aggregate/decide in-system; no human-feedback requirement (optional later).

================================================================
## 10. TUNING METHODOLOGY (DSO corpus = simulation/priming fixture, NOT a threshold source)
================================================================
rebar != DSO; DSO bands won't transfer. Use the DSO corpus to: (a) ground "how do we review THIS kind of ticket"
on representative real examples; (b) SIMULATE candidate rules over the corpus to see how they'd redistribute
tickets across review levels (over/under-review check); (c) prime the chunk-size + threshold experiments with
real inputs. The DSO complexity labels are unvalidated evaluator OUTPUT — one input among many, never ground
truth. Set our defaults from experiments + simulation, then re-derive per client from live REVIEW_RESULT data.

================================================================
## 11. FOLLOW-ON REGISTER (tracked SEPARATELY from this epic)
================================================================
F1. FP/dismissal + remediation-rate TRACKING across review cycles (the offline analysis tooling on #9 data).
F2. AUTO-DEMOTE a blocking criterion past an FP ceiling (depends on F1).
F3. CONFIDENCE/SEVERITY floor for blocking findings (fine-tuning on usage data).
F4. PROMOTE more checks to blocking-by-default as low-FP ones are observed (depends on F1).
F5. Project CONFIGURATION TOOL/UX (risk posture, thresholds, chunking, per-criteria blocking).
F6. BUG-ticket review (bugs shipped SKIPPED; dedicated follow-on epic; different shape from planning tickets).
F7. Cross-ticket NO-OVERLAP / DEPENDENCY-AWARE *semantic* detection (deterministic file-impact/link overlap is
    in-scope; semantic backlog-scan duplication -> follow-on).
F8. Project-SUPPLIED review criteria (registry future seam) + PROJECT-INVARIANT compliance (house rules).
F9. CODE-DRIFT invalidation (re-review when referenced code changes underneath; scope (i) now, drift later).
F10. CALIBRATED ABSTENTION + a labeled GOLD set (if/when attainable).
F11. RIGOR-SIGNATURE CHAIN / CI integration beyond exposing the signed result (helpers, conventions, more
     workflow signatures).
F12. SEVERITY-MINOR-FLOOR + NOT-FLAG tuning (per-criterion "what's minor"; needs usage data).
(In-scope-but-improves-later: centrality + blast-radius computed at plan time for escalation now; persisted as a
labeled tuning corpus = the follow-on benefit.)

================================================================
## 12. OPEN / PENDING APPROVAL
================================================================
- Proportionate-depth thresholds + escalation weights (default to be set from experiment/simulation; Joe approves posture).
- Budget posture (per-plan cap; INDETERMINATE-blocks-claim default = non-blocking; Joe approves).
- Confirm bug-skip + follow-on epic (F6).
- NEXT after sign-off: decompose this design into the rebar implementation epic (one wave, tasks with deps),
  tracked in rebar; create the follow-on register items (F1-F12) as separate linked tickets (discovered_from).

comments.body:
=== EXPERIMENT PROMPT (run in a fresh session) ===

Run a grounding experiment for the rebar plan-review gate we designed. Full design context is in rebar session
log `63cc-ec94-4792-464b` — run `rebar show 63cc-ec94-4792-464b` and read the entry titled "DESIGN OF RECORD:
plan-of-record-v4.md"; §5 is the criteria registry, §4 is the feedback-authoring spec, §6 is the
chunking/budget/proportionate-scrutiny model. The epic is `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa`.

GOAL: ground two defaults in real observed outcomes — (1) the CHUNKING strategy (how many Layer-2 review criteria
to batch per LLM call before result quality degrades) and (2) the BUDGET posture (cost + latency distribution per
review, to set a generous-but-grounded cap and a sense of where the INDETERMINATE/budget-cap outcome would
trigger). You are authorized to run ~100 experiment runs via subagents (a Workflow or subagent fan-out is fine).
This is a SIMULATION of the not-yet-built gate: a reviewer subagent applies a CHUNK of our Layer-2 advisory
criteria to a ticket's plan and returns structured findings authored to the §4 feedback spec (grounded in a
criterion/file/section, specific + actionable, severity-ranked, checklist-form).

INPUTS:
- Real plans from the DSO ticket store, READ-ONLY, at ~/digital-service-orchestra (an event-sourced rebar-like
  store: orphan `tickets` git branch and/or `.tickets-tracker/<ticket-id>/.cache.json`; a ticket's `description`
  + `acceptance_criteria`/comments are its "plan"). Select a STRATIFIED sample of ~5-6 real tickets spanning
  complexity — trivial task, moderate task/story, complex / epic-with-children — using size signals (AC count,
  children count, description length; note DSO `file_impact` is empty so don't rely on it). Cite the real ticket
  ids you pick.
- Our own epic `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa` (`rebar show`) as a DOGFOOD target — review it with our criteria too.

METHOD (≈100 runs):
- Apply only the LAYER-2 advisory/judgment criteria (chunking is about how many of those batch per LLM call; the
  Layer-1 deterministic checks are tool-based and out of scope for this experiment).
- Vary CHUNK SIZE across {1, 3, 6, ALL} criteria per reviewer call.
- For each (ticket × chunk size) run the reviewer subagent and REPEAT 5× to measure non-determinism.
  ~5 tickets × 4 chunk sizes × 5 repeats = 100 runs (adjust to land near 100; include the epic as one target).
- Use chunk-size = 1 (one criterion per call) as the QUALITY BASELINE. Do NOT tell the reviewer subagent that
  chunk size is the variable.

MEASURE per run: the findings (criterion, location, severity), token cost, wall-clock. Then COMPARE each coarser
chunk against the per-criterion baseline for the same ticket:
  (a) RECALL — does batching cause the reviewer to drop/dilute criteria the baseline catches?
  (b) NOISE — does it add spurious/duplicate findings?
  (c) CONSISTENCY — variance across the 5 repeats (non-determinism).
The chunk size at which recall drops or noise/variance rises materially vs the baseline = the degradation point;
the recommended default is the LARGEST chunk before that.

DELIVER (append to session log `63cc-ec94-4792-464b` AND save to a file):
  1. The observed quality-degradation point + a recommended DEFAULT chunk size (and whether it varies by ticket complexity).
  2. The cost + latency distribution (p50/p95) per review and per complexity tier -> a recommended GENEROUS budget
     cap (comfortably covers ~p95 + headroom, per the "generous to gather data" posture) and where INDETERMINATE would trigger.
  3. The DOGFOOD review of epic `5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa` — what our criteria flag about it (a real data point + a

  4. Honest caveats: DSO is ONE ticket-creation style, not representative of rebar's diverse client base, and this
     SIMULATES the system rather than running the real one — so treat outputs as grounded starting defaults, not final.

CONSTRAINTS: do NOT mutate the DSO ticket store (read-only). The reviewer subagent must be a different instance
