comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== EXPERIMENT RESULT: chunking + budget grounding (919 LLM runs, Sonnet-4.6) ===

GROUNDING EXPERIMENT COMPLETE. Two batches, 919 reviewer calls, 0 terminal errors, ≈ $25.71.
Full writeup committed at docs/experiments/plan-review-chunking-budget.md; raw data + harnesses under
docs/experiments/data/ (runs.jsonl, runs2.jsonl, harness.py, batch2.py, analyze*.py, criteria.json).
SIMULATION: single Sonnet-4.6 reviewer applies the 12 Layer-2 advisory criteria (F1,F4,E1,E2,E3,E5,E6,G5,
E4,G1G2,A1,COH) to a real ticket's plan, authored to §4 spec. Inputs READ-ONLY from DSO + dogfood epic 5fd2.
Batch1 = 5 tickets × chunk{1,3,6,12} × 5 repeats (100 cells). Batch2 = 6 tickets × criteria-per-turn
N{2,4,6,8,10,12} × 2 RANDOM partitions × 2 repeats (+N=1 solo) — random groupings decouple size from grouping.

HEADLINE FINDINGS
1) BATCHING DOES NOT DROP CRITERIA. Recall of solo-flagged criteria = 100% at EVERY N up to 12. Even
   all-12-in-one-call keeps every finding the per-criterion baseline produced. The design's central worry
   (coarse chunking dilutes recall) is NOT supported on this corpus.
2) The real cost of batching is (a) lower run-to-run CONSISTENCY (pooled Jaccard 0.70 @N=2 → 0.47–0.59 @N≥4)
   and (b) more OVER-FLAGGING vs solo (specificity 0.89 @N=2 → ~0.75 @N≥4). BOTH appear by N≈4 then PLATEAU —
   they do not keep worsening 4→12 in aggregate.
3) LARGE/COMPLEX plans destabilize at HIGH N specifically: container_epic Jaccard 1.0 @sizes 1/3/6 →
   0.33–0.40 @N=10–12 (whole reviews flip to 0 findings); dogfood_epic size-12 stdev 1.6 (a run collapsed to 0).
   Small/moderate plans tolerate high N fine. The all-at-once cliff is PLAN-SIZE-DEPENDENT.
4) Some "over-flagging" is LEGITIMATE context-dependence: cross-cutting criteria fire MORE with siblings visible
   (E5 testing 0.03 solo → 0.33–0.50 batched; COH 0.00 → 0.50). Reviewing them in ISOLATION under-fires them →
   argues against N=1 for cross-cutting criteria.

GROUNDED DEFAULT — CHUNKING / "criteria per turn / number of agents"
- DEFAULT = 4 criteria per turn = 3 parallel LLM calls per 12-criterion review (the knee: specificity+consistency
  already plateaued, recall intact, ~2× cheaper than N=2).
- Scale: trivial/moderate → 6–8 per turn (2 turns); complex/has-children/epic → 2–3 per turn (4–6 turns);
  weak/local models → ≤3. NEVER all-12-in-one for epic/large plans (the one clear quality cliff). Frontier
  Sonnet's stable ceiling for BIG plans ≈ 6; for small plans effectively 12.

GROUNDED DEFAULT — BUDGET
- Full-review tokens by N: N=1 p50 51k/p95 up-to-72k(big epic); N=2 25k/39k; N=4(default) 15k/21k; N=6 11k/16k;
  N=12 7k/10k. Per-tier @N=4 p95: trivial 8.6k · moderate 9.2k · small_epic 14k · dogfood 18k · complex_leaf
  18.5k · container_epic 22k. Parallel wall-clock p50 ~34–60s; worst single call p95 ~88s.
- GENEROUS CAP = ~90k tokens + ~240s per plan (covers even a big epic at the FINEST N=1, p95 ~72k, + headroom →
  never clips a legit review). Typical envelope ~15–25k / 40–60s (telemetry). INDETERMINATE triggers: cap-hit
  mid-review (checkpoint between chunks, shed lowest-priority, never silent PASS — at 90k essentially never fires
  = intended generous behavior); chunk error after retries (0/919 here); top-tier sound-tool unavailable.

DOGFOOD — epic 5fd2 reviewed by our own criteria (5/5 repeats, consistent):
- G5 decomposition MAJOR conf 0.95 5/5 FAIL: "epic but NO child tickets; 12 ACs span 8–10 distinct deliverables"
  — EXACTLY the predicted "decompose into children" finding.
- E5 testing MAJOR conf 0.92 5/5: "the plan has no testing plan" for the gate itself.
- E2/E1/E6/F1 MINOR 4–5/5: chunking/budget/depth defaults DEFERRED to external experiment results rather than
  inlined (ambiguity/orphan-AC/end-state). THIS EXPERIMENT CLOSES THAT GAP — folding the numbers above resolves it.
- E4 MINOR: "solidlsp already in repo", "reuse rebar.llm catalog/runner" asserted — verify before relying.

CAVEATS (honest): DSO = ONE creation style, not representative (absolute flag-rates won't transfer; the CURVE
SHAPES do). SIMULATION from plan-text only — codebase-grounded criteria (E4/G1G2/A1) ≈0.00 solo AND batched
(no repo access); their real tool-grounded chunking economics UNTESTED here. No ground-truth labels (recall =
vs-solo, noise = over-flag-vs-solo; consistency is the trustworthy axis). Single model. G3/G4 child-coverage
excluded → container path under-tested.

NEXT (per the prompt — second validation round before locking): (a) non-DSO corpora / other creation styles;
(b) run codebase-grounded criteria with real repo access; (c) a weaker model to locate its stable-N ceiling.
THEN: fold these defaults into epic 5fd2 §6/§12 (resolving its own E2/E6/F1 self-flag) + decompose into the
implementation wave + file F1–F12 as discovered_from-linked tickets.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== EXPERIMENT RESULT (round 2): Opus-vs-Sonnet model tradeoff + intentional grouping (460 runs) ===

Follow-up to the chunking/budget grounding. Answers: (1) how many criteria can OPUS handle/turn without
degradation; (2) $/criterion Opus-vs-Sonnet at each model's max stable N; (3) does intentional COHERENT grouping
raise Sonnet's reliable ceiling. 460 calls, 0 errors, ≈$22.7 (Opus $16.3 + Sonnet $6.3). Pricing (authoritative,
via claude-api skill): Opus 4.8 $5/$25 per M, Sonnet 4.6 $3/$15 per M (Opus ~1.67×/token). Writeup committed at
docs/experiments/plan-review-model-tradeoff.md; raw data + harnesses under docs/experiments/data/
(runs3_opus.jsonl, runs4_group.jsonl, batch3_opus.py, batch4_grouping.py, analyze3.py). Thinking OFF for both
models (like-for-like). Exp A = 5 tickets × N{2,4,6,8,12} × 2 random partitions × 2 repeats on Opus (mirrors the
Sonnet batch2). Exp B = 6 tickets × {coherent, anti} grouping × N{4,6} × 3 repeats on Sonnet, vs batch2's random.

R1 — OPUS DOES NOT DEGRADE AS N GROWS; SONNET DOES.
Pooled run-to-run consistency (Jaccard of FAIL-sets): Sonnet 0.70(N2)→0.53→0.47→0.56→0.59(N12) — peaks at 2,
falls after ~3. Opus 0.61→0.61→0.60→0.56→0.67 — FLAT-to-rising, most consistent at N=12. So Opus's reliable
ceiling ≈ the full set (~12 criteria/turn); Sonnet's ≈ 2–3. Opus also avoids Sonnet's big-plan flip (container
epic @N=12: Sonnet 3↔0 flips J0.33; Opus stable). Caveat: neither is uniformly stable at 12 on EVERY plan (Opus
noisier on the complex leaf @12, J0.42; returns 0 on the container epic — stable but maybe under-flagging). Keep
chunk <12 on the LARGEST plans for both; the flat-vs-falling SHAPE is the transferable result.

R2 — ONE OPUS CALL BEATS MANY RELIABLE SONNET CALLS, ON COST *AND* RELIABILITY.
$/criterion at each model's stable setting: Sonnet @N=2 (stable region) $0.0123/crit, $0.147/review (6 calls,
plan re-sent 6×). Opus @N=12 (stable max) $0.0086/crit, $0.103/review (1 call, plan sent once). The per-TOKEN
premium (1.67×) INVERTS per REVIEW because Opus amortizes the plan+system once while a reliable Sonnet review
needs 4–6 small calls. → One Opus pass is ~30% CHEAPER per criterion than reliable Sonnet AND more consistent.
Sonnet is cheaper in absolute terms only at N=12 ($0.057/review) — the config that's UNSTABLE on big plans. So
"many cheap Sonnet agents" is a FALSE ECONOMY at the reliable setting.

R3 — COHERENT GROUPING ~TRIPLES SONNET'S RELIABLE CRITERIA-PER-TURN.
Sonnet consistency by grouping: coherent 0.71(N4)/0.70(N6); random 0.53/0.47; anti 0.79/0.66. COHERENT@6 (0.70)
MATCHES RANDOM@2 (0.70) → clustering criteria by the plan facet they examine lets Sonnet reliably review ~6
criteria/turn at the consistency random only reaches at 2 (~3× lift), WITHOUT suppressing findings (coherent
flag-rate 0.25–0.26 ≈ random 0.25–0.27). Anti-affinity also raises Jaccard but partly by UNDER-flagging (0.21 →
recall loss) — not a clean win. MECHANISM/CAVEAT: part of random's lower consistency is that its instances mix 2
DIFFERENT partitions (grouping varies); coherent/anti hold ONE fixed partition across repeats. That IS the
actionable finding: the gate should use a FIXED, declared grouping, not random chunking — fixing the partition is
most of the win, affinity clustering preserves recall on top.

RECOMMENDATIONS (fold into epic 5fd2 §6 + chunking-config schema):
(1) MODEL-TIERED CHUNKING: frontier (Opus) → up to 12/turn (1 call); mid (Sonnet) → 6/turn IF coherently grouped,
    else ≤3; weak/local → ≤3. (R1's "Sonnet ≤3" holds only for UNGROUPED chunking.)
(2) PREFER ONE OPUS PASS as the high-reliability default — cheaper per criterion than reliable Sonnet + more
    consistent. Reserve Sonnet small-chunk for the cost floor on small/simple plans (coherent N=6, $0.079/review).
(3) CHUNKING CONFIG MUST SPECIFY A FIXED, COHERENT PARTITION (criteria clustered by plan facet) — not random.
(4) BUDGET (updated): generous cap ≈ $0.30 / ~25k tokens per plan; typical Opus one-pass ≈ $0.10 / 9–15k tokens;
    typical reliable Sonnet ≈ $0.08–0.15. INDETERMINATE triggers unchanged.

CAVEATS carry over: DSO=one style; plan-text-only (codebase-grounded E4/G1G2/A1 barely fire); no ground-truth
labels (consistency is the trustworthy axis); thinking OFF (adaptive would shift quality+cost, untested); weak/
local model ceiling still unmeasured.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
=== EXPERIMENT RESULT (round 3): criteria reconciliation + substance + agentic tier → storage/chunking design ===

Addresses Joe's challenge: (1) verify our criteria set + that experiments used substantive not bare-bones
criteria; (2) confirm single-turn vs agentic (tool-use); (3) >12 criteria; (4) model+size-aware chunk-size
defaults; (5) facet-based criteria storage for advisory grouping that scales/stays fresh. Two new experiments
(Sonnet, +real codebase tools, ≈$5). Design committed at
docs/experiments/plan-review-criteria-storage-and-chunking.md; DSO-grounded criterion specs at
docs/experiments/data/dso-criteria-specs.md; data/harnesses under docs/experiments/data/ (criteria_v2.json,
exp1_substance.*, exp2_agentic.*, analyze4.py). Epic 5fd2 description updated with a "## Experiment-grounded
defaults" section + the deferred-defaults AC checked (still passes check_ac + clarity 7).

RECONCILIATION (Joe was right on all counts):
- My round 1-2 experiments tested a THIN, SINGLE-TURN-ONLY subset (~12) with BARE-BONES one-liners. The real v4
  §5 registry spans FOUR EXEC TIERS and is larger: DET (P1-P7), SINGLE-TURN (F1,F4,E2,E5,G5 + 2-STEP E1,E3,E6),
  AGENT/tool-using (E4,G1G2,A1,T1,T6,T7,T8), triggered overlays (T5a-e + others). Mined DSO for the FULL
  specs (real binary checklists + severity + anti-FP, cited file:line) → criteria_v2.json (12 single-turn) +
  dso-criteria-specs.md (all tiers incl agentic + overlays).

THREE CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER ROUNDS:
1. EXEC TIER is the PRIMARY axis, not chunk size. DET=parallel code (~free). SINGLE-TURN=chunkable (~$0.005-0.008
   /criterion cached). AGENT=one tool-loop per criterion, ~$0.12 + ~50s, ~15 tool calls (≈85× single-turn) —
   NOT chunkable. So chunking applies ONLY within the single-turn tier; agentic = 1-agent-each, gated by
   proportionate scrutiny.
2. "COARSE CHUNKS ARE CHEAPER" was a NO-CACHING artifact. With prompt caching (plan read at 0.1×), the cost gap
   between chunk sizes collapses 2.6×→1.55× (N=2 $0.090 vs N=12 $0.058/review). Fine chunking is NOT expensive →
   within single-turn, chunk for RELIABILITY not cost. Also narrows Opus's one-pass edge: cached fine-chunk Sonnet
   ($0.07-0.09) ≈ one Opus pass ($0.10).
3. SUBSTANCE doesn't lower the reliable chunk size — fully-specified criteria are MORE consistent at coarse N than
   one-liners (Jaccard N=4 0.61 vs 0.53; N=12 0.65 vs 0.59). Explicit checklists cut reviewer variance. Round-1/2
   chunk-size guidance is safe.

EXP2 AGENTIC (the single-turn-vs-agent answer, with REAL tools over rebar+DSO repos): E4/G1G2/A1 each ~15 tool
calls / ~9 iters / ~50s / ~$0.12. With tools they flip AMBIGUOUS→grounded — G1G2 caught our OWN epic's "solidlsp
(already in repo)" claim is FALSE (glob finds zero; solidlsp is a Serena dep, not committed). Real dogfood win the
no-tool runs could only mark AMBIGUOUS.

DESIGN DELIVERED:
- STORAGE: criterion descriptor gains exec(tier) + facet(concern/context — the advisory grouping key) +
  context_needs + routing + trigger. Generic chunker: filter→bucket by tier→pack same-facet single-turn criteria
  to chunk size→1 agent per AGENT criterion→DET as code. Adding/tuning a criterion only declares exec+facet (no
  hand-maintained chunk lists) — grouping advisory (re-packs at any chunk size). Facets are the CONCERN not
  arbitrary (Joe's instinct): ac-text-quality{F1,E2,E6}, scope-intent{F4,E3,G5}, coherence{E1}, testing{E5},
  codebase-grounding{E4,G1G2,A1}, overlay-* per concern.
- CHUNK SIZE FORMULA (single-turn tier): base_chunk{opus 12, sonnet 6 coherent / 3 plain, haiku/local 3} ×
  size_factor{trivial/moderate 1.0, large|epic|has_children 0.5}, clamp[2,n]. → Opus all-in-one cached call;
  Sonnet 6(coherent)/3(large); never full set on largest plans.
- BUDGET: cap = $0.15 base + n_agentic×$0.25 + headroom (small ~$0.15-0.40; heavy epic ~$1.5-2.0+minutes). Enable
  caching. INDETERMINATE sheds AGENT/overlay first (85× cost), never the cheap base.

NEXT: fold schema (exec/facet) + formula + per-tier budget into plan-of-record §5-§6; decompose into impl wave;
file F1-F12. Optional validation: non-DSO corpora; a weaker/local model's stable-N; tighter agentic loop / Haiku
sub-agent to lower the $0.12 agentic floor.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
Brainstorm + plan-of-record for epic gnu-whale-ichor (e68d-b701-4dd9-47aa), "Authenticated identity".

OBJECTIVE (clarified by Joe): give rebar a modeled identity for the user running it, to enable (1) accurate Jira (later GitHub) user mapping, (2) optional per-project requirement of an authenticated identity attributing changes to a real user (defaulting to the GitHub committer), (3) zero-config low friction for projects that don't opt in.

CHOSEN PATTERN: adopt git-bug's identity model wholesale (it is the strongest analog — event-sourced, git-backed, multi-clone) on rebar's existing event/ticket machinery (new `identity` ticket type, event-log-as-version-chain). One coherent trust family (self-managed keys + TOFU + offline). Gap-fills vs vanilla git-bug, none foreign:
- G1 SSHSIG instead of PGP (adoption + reuse GitHub SSH key); `ssh-keygen -Y sign/verify` over canonical bytes, namespace `rebar`; shell out (no maintained pure-Python SSHSIG verifier).
- G2 implement the signed identity-chain authorization git-bug stubbed (`IsProtected()` TODO): rotate/add/revoke keys must be signed by a currently-valid key; per-person 1-of-n (Keybase topology, NOT Radicle per-repo m-of-n).
- G3 opt-in project enforcement: local write-gate + CI/fsck verify (close-gate precedent).
- G4 availability: replay NEVER rejects (vs git-bug fail-close); mark verified|unverified|unsigned, CI fails policy.
- G6 compaction survival: SNAPSHOT + process_snapshot carry folded-event identity/sig.

DE-FRANKENSTEINED (cut after adversarial subagent critique): NO DSSE/Sigstore/keyless seam (different online/CA/OIDC trust model; YAGNI; canonical-bytes boundary preserves the option). NO active GitHub ssh_signing_keys social-proof in v1 (github-login stored as plain metadata; active proof is a follow-on). Relabel: it's git-bug ENTITY + Radicle SSHSIG SUBSTRATE + Keybase per-person TOPOLOGY — Radicle proves the substrate, not the (per-repo m-of-n) topology we reject.

TRUST-ROOT convergent four-layer recipe (Radicle/TUF/Keybase/Sigstore): (a) self-certifying genesis+TOFU, (b) signed chain authorized by current key set, (c) optional external attestation, (d) equivocation detection. rebar implements all four within one trust family.

JIRA IDENTITY INTEGRATION (given ACLI): reconciler uses official `acli jira workitem` (subprocess) + direct REST (acli_rest.py) for what acli can't do. Today only assignee syncs (bare string), no reporter, no per-user binding. Official acli has NO user-lookup and NO --reporter; --assignee takes email/accountId (server-side resolve). Reporter attribution needs direct REST (fields.reporter:{accountId}) + Modify Reporter permission, else falls back to bot. accountId is the only stable id; email privacy-gated/null; /user/search is prefix-match/unreliable — so the tool MUST maintain its own map. The `identity` entity IS that map (jira-accountId immutable metadata): outbound resolve identity→accountId, set assignee (acli/REST) + reporter (REST when permitted), bootstrap/repair via /user/search, degrade to -1/unassigned/bot. Inbound reverse-resolve accountId→identity, resolve-or-create auto-upgrading ghost. Provider-neutral (jira-accountId now, GitHub node-id later) so be74 reuses it.

Tiers: T0 unverified git-config author (DCO-style, default), T1 SSHSIG opt-in. Enforcement = local write-gate + CI/fsck; replay never rejects.

Research surveyed: git-bug, Radicle/Heartwood, Pijul, Keybase, TUF, Sigstore/gitsign, Fossil, Plane, Huly, OpenProject, Taiga, sourcehut, Bugzilla, GitLab/Gitea/Forgejo; SSHSIG/allowed_signers, GitHub ssh_signing_keys (forward-only, no reverse), DSSE/securesystemslib, ACLI (official + Bob Swift/Appfire).

OUT/follow-ons: DSSE/keyless+transparency (sibling security epic 8a1c), active github-login proof, full reconciler provider-generalization + GitHub Issues user sync (be74), reporter sync without Modify Reporter (documented degradation only).

alternative-selection (AGENT, the top gap; subsumes correctness+alternatives+fitness+the 7 DSO anti-patterns),
T10 infrastructure/IaC (Joe-requested; deterministic trigger), T11 data-migration/backfill safety, T12 rollout/

+ 7 anti-patterns) + approach-proposer (>=3 distinct on 4 axes) -> folded into G6. KEY: DSO validates our anti-priming
design - its task-decomposer gets ONLY the chosen approach ("do not re-architect"); rejected alternatives are
logged in-session, NEVER persisted to a ticket the implementer reads.

comments.body:
=== CORRECTION: the two "open design questions" were SETTLED in the brainstorm ===
The round-5 critical review re-raised (1) blocking-on-claim-vs-coaching and (2) what-the-signature-certifies. Both
were the brainstorm's CENTRAL debates (session log 63cc, DISCUSSION NARRATIVE comment 37 + final-decisions 38),
resolved with explicit reasoning - NOT open. (1) The brainstorm weighed A blocking-inline / B advisory / C
decoupled-signed-attestation and chose C: claim = FAST check for a signed 'ready' attestation, heavy review
out-of-band, --force escape; the 'hard-gate-is-anti-pattern' research was examined and found NOT to transfer to
autonomous agents (confabulate-not-ask; errors compound; separate-critic >> self-critique). (2) An Opus adversarial
review IN the brainstorm already raised the 'fail-open hollow signal' critique; resolution: cert = 'process followed,
no red flags' + COVERAGE recorded; rich per-criterion verdicts in the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar; CI composes any hard
gate from the signed result + coverage; block-by-default-with-routine-override explicitly REJECTED (>30% FP -> tool
ignored). Corrected epic 5fd2 (the 'Open design questions' section -> 'Design decisions revisited (SETTLED)'). The
genuinely-useful residual is tuning: state end-to-end time-to-first-work honestly; cache busts on edit-then-re-review;
make the CI rigor predicate canonical.

=== EXPERIMENT PLAN to finalize + tune (with a seeded-defect pilot) ===
The recurring gap (and the brainstorm's stated PRIMARY metric): we validated CONSISTENCY (Jaccard), never GROUND
TRUTH. Proposed prioritized plan (docs/experiments/plan-review-validation-experiment-plan.md): E1 seeded-defect
recall/false-accept gold set (top - the only thing that measures whether criteria CATCH what they should; promotes
F10 gold set into the pre-finalize loop); E2 baseline the never-run criteria (G6/T10/T11/T12/T1/T3/T4/T5d/G3/G4/COH);
E3 new-overlay trigger precision; E4 generalization on a NON-DSO corpus (answers the overfit critique); E5 weak/local
model ceiling; E6 G6 alternative-generation + anti-priming; E7 structured-checklist lift A/B.

PILOT (E1, 32 runs): seeded BAD/GOOD plan per criterion for G6/T10/T11/T12/E5/COH/T9/A1. RESULT: RECALL = 100% (8/8
BAD caught as FAIL, both repeats), ZERO rubber-stamping - the new criteria + roll-ins catch the defect they target

precision metric. Raw: plan-review-gate/runs/seedpilot.jsonl.

NEXT: expand E1 to 3-5 adjudicated cases per criterion (all 31) with the grounded ones tool-run -> the per-criterion
recall/false-accept/false-fire scorecard to finalize on; then E2/E4.

- The plan's DESIGN of T10 is internally consistent and experiment-grounded: T10 is LLM-routed for plan review (the "FINALIZE CORRECTION (E4-confirmed)" section grounds this — deterministic IaC keywords over-fired on the non-DSO corpus, LLM router fired 0 false), classified AGENT-tier (an IaC verdict depends on the actual `.tf`; the agent found a real committed secret a single-turn pass missed — `criteria_v8.json` `_tier_note`, line 1178), advisory by default (`block_threshold` 0.95), with the full seven binary sub-checks (state/IAM/idempotency/blast-radius/secrets/cost/observability) carried in `criteria_v8.json` (lines 1144-1172) and a `suppress_types:["bug"]` rule consistent with the epic's bug carve-out.

comments.body:
PASS-1 REVIEW (criterion T1 — Prior-art / novel-architecture justification) [overlay]

T1 bright-line FIRES (a novel architectural pattern: a plan-review verification gate firing at open→in_progress). The overlay therefore applies, and the plan handles all three T1 checks well overall.

AFFIRMATIONS (criteria passed):
- T1(a) prior-art considered / anti-reinvention: STRONG. The whole design is framed as the *inverse of an existing rebar feature* (the completion-verifier close gate) and is built ON four named prior epics rather than reinvented — three-pass framework `9da1`, workflow engine `e6d9`, prompt storage `da27`, grounding oracle `8f6c`. Layer-1 explicitly "does NOT add its own tool integrations… it CONSUMES the shipped oracle." Coaching/verdict mechanisms cite external prior art (Chain-of-Verification, FactScore/SAFE, RAGAS-faithfulness, TICK; lost-in-the-middle; anti-sycophancy; "external-grounded > self-reflection") plus ~30 research reports. This is the opposite of repackaging-without-consideration.
- T1(c) unverified capability assertions resolved: STRONG. The load-bearing "X is shipped, consume it" claims are GROUNDED — the `refute_absence`/`applies`/`scan` oracle facade exists at src/rebar/grounding/ (verified: src/rebar/grounding/__init__.py, oracle.py, resolve.py) and is already consumed by src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py. The cap=10 / chunking / tier defaults are honestly labeled "experiment-informed but INCONCLUSIVE ALONE / tune from dogfood data," not asserted as validated constants — the right posture for an unproven assertion.

The single finding below is minor coaching, not a blocker.

- [ ] State the prior-art / "why not an off-the-shelf agentic-eval framework" rationale for the gate's own novel three-pass + Pass-4-coach pipeline as explicitly as it is stated for the consumed prerequisites. (criteria: T1; T1(b) novelty-justification. location: "Design summary" / "Review structure — three-pass" sections.) The plan justifies the INVERSE-of-close-gate framing and grounds the verdict MECHANISM in research, but the higher-level architectural choice — a bespoke 4-pass (find→verify→deterministic-gate→coach) review pipeline rather than an existing agentic-eval/LLM-judge harness (e.g. the Inspect-AI / promptfoo seams the plan already wires into, or G-Eval/LLM-as-judge rubric runners) — is asserted via the `9da1` adoption rather than weighed against those alternatives. evidence: the plan adopts the three-pass design "from epic 9da1" and the Pass-4 coach is novel-by-construction (locked move-registry templates), but no section says "we considered an off-the-shelf judge/eval pipeline and chose a custom one because…". This is a Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging gap only at the pipeline-shape level; the per-pass mechanisms are well-grounded. suggested_fix: (empty — defer to author; the rationale likely lives in session log 63cc but isn't surfaced in this self-contained epic summary.)
